pages.text: The river had dropped below ankle height. White shells dotted the ground. Each child came out with a bowl.
Sonu raised their bowl. "I'll fill mine, too!" But small hands picked up only one shell at a time.
That evening, three bowls stood together in the room. Sonu's had the fewest.
At night, Sonu quietly got up and moved shells from Mina's bowl into their own.
Sonu held their breath and reached out. In the dark, the bowls were hard to see.
A hand slipped. Crash! Shells spilled over the floor.
By morning, all the shells were mixed together. Sonu looked at the empty bowls, unable to say anything.
Mom picked up one shell and gently placed it in Sonu's bowl.
"I spilled them while moving them. I'm sorry." Sonu spoke. Mina shared the shells equally among the three.
Sonu carried their bowl to the riverbank. This time, their own hands picked up more, one by one. Shells piled softly inside.
